d23c4292-6fdd-5cba-a2e7-0f4d770b2309.title: Finding the Least-Squares Solution of a Linear System Given in Matrix Form

e-5589.knowledge_point: Finding the Least-Squares Solution of a Linear System Given in Matrix Form
e-5589.problem:
Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the least-squares solution of $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$, where 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071086/assets/8b006c23e83405be4cd93396e5bde38c0dbcb5f8bb735b125d0b05f439e5b0d9.png)
e-5589.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $A \mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}\mathbin{:}$
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071086/assets/6fed2ac5452cf11059550a0c6328914c0e897714ca14a68f71df8eeb6d93471d.png)

We can find the least-squares solution ${\hat{\mathbf{x}}}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by $A^T\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix $A^T \! A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $(A^T \! A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\,\,\,[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}6 & -3 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ -\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

before.name: Question 1
before.problem:

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the least-squares solution of $Ax=b$, where 

$\,$ $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 15\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{45}[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{45}[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Least-Squares Solution of a Linear System Given in Matrix Form
content.problem:
Given that the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, find the least-squares solution of $Ax=b$, where 

$\,$ $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
First of all, we write the given system in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]}}\overset{x}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}}
$$

We can find the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{x}$ of the equation above by solving the corresponding normal equation, which we obtain by left-multiplying our original equation by ${A}^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A\overset{^}{x} & ={A}^{T}b\end{aligned}
$$

Since the columns of $A$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A$ is invertible. Therefore, multiplying by $({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}$ on the left, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{x} & =({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}{A}^{T}b \\  & ={([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 15\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{45}[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{45}[\begin{aligned}15 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 2
?

Given that the columns of A are linearly independent, find the least-squares solution of Ax=b, where

A=[1021−1−110011−1] and b=[6060].

a
[032]
b
[320]
c
[302]
d
[203]
e
[12012]
Submit

decision.explanation: The columns are orthogonal, so A^T A = diag(4,2,6). Also, A^T b = (12,0,12)^T. Solving the normal equations gives the least-squares solution (3,0,2)^T, which is option c.
